analysis.investment_thesis: PhysicsWallah scores near-zero on both Magic Formula metrics — Earnings Yield of ~0.6% (EBIT INR 199 Cr / EV ~INR 31,919 Cr) and negative ROCE of -2.12%, making it untouchable under any value-based framework. Exceptional revenue growth (131% CAGR) is entirely offset by an absurd valuation (EV/EBITDA 433x) and a track record of destroying capital over the past three years.
key_strengths: Explosive revenue growth: INR 233 Cr (2022) → INR 2,887 Cr (2025), 131% CAGR — genuine brand resonance in Indian ed-tech
OCF turned consistently positive (4/4 years), with FY2025 OCF of INR 507 Cr and FCF of INR 340 Cr showing some cash generation
High promoter holding (72.3%) signals founder conviction; FII/DII combined 25% suggests institutional validation
key_risks: Near-zero earnings yield (~0.6%) — EV of ~INR 31,919 Cr against EBIT of only INR 199 Cr makes this one of the most expensive stocks in any screen
Serial capital destruction: cumulative net losses of INR 1,458 Cr over FY2023-25, equity was negative for two consecutive years (-INR 183 Cr, -INR 1,246 Cr)
Massive uninvestigated investing outflows: -INR 1,513 Cr in FY2025 investing CF with no clear return — FY2024's -INR 672 Cr 'other income' suggests prior acquisition impairments
red_flags: Earnings Yield of 0.62% — Magic Formula requires >12% to even consider
ROCE of -2.12% and ROE of -17.38% — capital is being destroyed, not compounded
Equity turned negative twice (2023, 2024) — balance sheet required a large capital infusion to survive
FY2024 net loss of INR 1,131 Cr driven by -INR 672 Cr other income — likely goodwill impairment from poorly-priced acquisitions
Borrowings spiked from zero to INR 2,461 Cr then collapsed to INR 970 Cr in one year — erratic and opaque capital structure
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Through the Magic Formula lens, PhysicsWallah fails both tests catastrophically. Earnings Yield (EBIT/EV) = 199 / 31,919 = 0.62% — against my 12% minimum threshold. Return on Capital is negative per the reported ROCE of -2.12%, confirmed by three consecutive years of net losses totaling INR 1,458 Cr. The EV/EBITDA of 433x is not a typo — the market is pricing in decades of future profits that have yet to materialize. The Magic Formula explicitly requires BOTH cheapness AND business quality; PWL has neither today.

The revenue story is genuinely impressive — 131% CAGR is rare — and OCF of INR 507 Cr in FY2025 shows the underlying subscription/course model can generate cash. But this is a story stock, not a value stock. The balance sheet required a complete rescue: equity went from -INR 1,246 Cr (FY2024) to +INR 1,398 Cr (FY2025), almost certainly via the IPO. Continued heavy investing outflows (-INR 1,513 Cr in FY2025) suggest management is still in aggressive expansion mode with no demonstrated ability to earn above cost of capital. I'd revisit only if EBIT/EV exceeds 12% and ROCE sustains above 20% for two full fiscal years — both are years away at minimum.
